title: The Grand Aurora Hotel
description: Scope: deployment overview. Cell services and Aurora clusters are aggregates, not single-AZ instances. The companion views expand identity/isolation and one pooled cell’s availability/recovery design. They are authored views, not automatic projections. Assumptions: tenant onboarding writes an authoritative tenant-to-cell directory; discovery returns an endpoint to the browser. Each cell independently verifies identity, tenant assignment and membership. Discovery is not a trusted authorization shortcut. The enterprise account has separate credentials, application resources and database. Pooled isolation additionally needs transaction-local validated tenant context, a non-owner database role, forced row-level policies and tests for bypass paths. Provisioning uses an allowlisted cross-account role and CloudFormation. Organization-trail coverage, central bucket policy, KMS permissions and retention must be configured; API audit capture is not application-log capture. No deployed configuration is supplied.

edges.meaning: Staff presents issued JWT; discovery verifies issuer, audience and tenant membership.
Resolve validated tenant to its cell; directory is not an authorization bypass.
Return pooled-cell API endpoint to the browser; not a server proxy request.
Return enterprise-cell API endpoint to the browser; each cell reauthorizes the tenant.
API private integration reaches application tasks; VPC Link and internal ALB are expanded in the identity view.
Transactional booking access with server-derived tenant context and database policies.
Dedicated API private integration reaches its own application service; same-account network detail is expanded separately.
Separate account and database isolate the enterprise data plane.
Provisioner assumes a tightly scoped cross-account deployment role.
Assumed role authorizes CloudFormation in the dedicated account.
Stack owns cell resources; arrow summarizes provisioning, not runtime traffic.
AWS API activity is captured by the configured organization trail, not application log streaming.
Organization coverage includes the enterprise account; application logs are separate.
Central S3 delivery requires organization-trail bucket and encryption-key policies.
